correctness.rationale: Since \(m\mid p+1\), the index-\(m\) subgroup \(H\) contains \(\mathbb F_p^\times\), and \(|H/\mathbb F_p^\times|=(p+1)/m\). For a character descending nontrivially to that quotient, decompose \(H\) into prime-field projective lines. The canonical additive-character sum over a line is \(p-1\) on the unique trace-zero line and \(-1\) otherwise. Quotient-character orthogonality then forces each compressed Fourier entry to vanish unless its product orbit is the distinguished trace-zero orbit, where it equals \(p\chi(t_0)\). Hence there is exactly one nonzero entry per row and column, all of modulus \(p\), giving determinant modulus \(p^m\), \(m^2-m\) zero entries, and exactly \((p+1)/m-1\) eligible nontrivial characters. Fresh checks confirmed the subgroup and character-count boundary at \(p=7,m=4\); the universal conclusion rests on the projective-line proof.
